title: Fifty days of Easter
hookLine: Easter lasts until Pentecost; the alleluia returns
tomorrow: Holy days and the saints' calendar

cards: Easter Sunday: the eggs, the lamb, the big lunch, the chocolate, the cousins asleep on the couch. By Monday the decorations are in a box. By Tuesday it's back to normal, and Easter feels like it came and went in a day.
Meanwhile the Church is just getting started. For six weeks it gave things up. Now, on the calendar it keeps, the party runs for seven weeks.

teach.b: For Catholics, Easter isn't a day. It's a season, fifty days long, from Easter Sunday to Pentecost.
It opens with the octave: eight days, each kept as if it were Easter Sunday itself, with the Gloria every day and a double alleluia at the dismissal.
On the fortieth day, or where it's moved, the Sunday after, the Church remembers the Ascension, because the Acts of the Apostles says the risen Jesus appeared to his friends over forty days.
On the fiftieth comes Pentecost, simply Greek for fiftieth, the day the Holy Spirit came. The arithmetic is on purpose. Lent is forty days.
Easter is fifty. The feast is longer than the fast. And the season's sound is the word that went missing.

All through Lent, Catholics don't say or sing alleluia at Mass. Some old customs even said goodbye to it before Lent, and in a few places, tradition says, people buried a scroll with the word written on it.
Now it's back everywhere, doubled and tripled. Alleluia is Hebrew: hallelu, praise, and Yah, a short form of God's name.

It passed into Greek and Latin untranslated, and it's still said in its original form in churches around the world. A few more things change for fifty days. The tall Easter candle from the vigil is lit at every Mass.

At noon, in place of the Angelus, the custom is the Regina Caeli: Queen of Heaven, rejoice. And everything of the last weeks, the ashes, the stations, the towel on Thursday, the fire on Saturday, was pointing here.

how: Catholics keep Easter as a fifty-day season ending at Pentecost: the Easter candle burns at Mass, the alleluia is sung again, the Regina Caeli replaces the Angelus, and the first eight days are each celebrated like Easter Sunday.

games.q: what's inside the season — tap the pairs.
p: eight days kept like Easter Sunday

s: for Catholics, Easter is over by Monday
Easter is a season of fifty days, running to Pentecost.
the Easter season is longer than Lent
Lent is forty days; Easter is fifty. the feast outlasts the fast.
it's Hebrew, praise Yah, carried into Greek and Latin untranslated.

games.q: it's noon on a Tuesday in the Easter season, and you usually pray the Angelus. what is the custom instead?
o: the Regina Caeli, Queen of Heaven, rejoice.
nothing: the Angelus stops for Easter.
games.why: for the fifty days, the custom is to pray the Regina Caeli at noon in place of the Angelus, a short Easter prayer to Mary full of alleluias.

practice: Say alleluia out loud, even quietly, even if it feels odd in your kitchen: once, then again a little slower, listening to the sound of it.

Think of one thing in your life right now worth praise: one person, one mercy, one ordinary good thing. If you pray, offer it to God as that single word; if you don't, let it be a word of gladness, and sit with the quiet after it.

wordCard.voice: Alleluia. Hebrew for praise Yah, the word that disappears for Lent and comes back doubled through the fifty days of Easter. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: praise Yah (a short form of God's name). passed into Greek and Latin untranslated.

carryVoice: Your line: longer than lent. The word that went missing is back for all fifty days. See you tomorrow.
